pages.text: When <name> received the message, he almost dropped his lunchbox. “Congratulations! You’ve been chosen to represent Earth at the Interplanetary Science Fair on Jupiter’s moon, Europa.” His mother blinked. “That’s wonderful, beta! But finish your idli first.”

A week later, wearing a silver science suit and holding a glowing lunchbox of homemade samosas, <name> boarded the space shuttle Aryabhatta II. As the engines roared, Earth shrank into a blue marble below him.
When he landed on Europa, his jaw dropped. The fairgrounds floated in domes of shimmering glass. Alien kids from every corner of the galaxy displayed inventions that buzzed, sparkled, and danced.

A green, jelly-like creature named Zilo showed off talking plants that recited poetry. A three-eyed Martian kid had teleporting snacks that kept vanishing mid-bite. And <name>? He proudly set up his project — the “Kindness Communicator,” a device that turned emotions into colors and music.
“Whoa,” said a furry alien with six fingers. “What’s that tune?” “It’s joy,” <name> said, grinning. “Like when you share your lunch with a friend.”
The fair was going perfectly — until alarms blared. A solar flare from Jupiter’s storms was heading straight for the fair! Lights flickered. Machines froze. Floating domes began to lose power.

Panic spread among the young scientists. Zilo’s talking plants started yelling nonsense. The teleporting snacks flew everywhere. But <name> stayed calm. “Everyone, listen! If we link all our inventions together, we can rebuild the power grid.”

He used his Kindness Communicator to coordinate. The aliens hummed, whistled, and sent signals in their own ways. A Martian used magnet pods to stabilize circuits. Zilo’s plants produced oxygen for the flickering domes.
Finally, with teamwork and a spark of creativity, the power returned. The domes glowed brighter than ever, filled with laughter and music.

When the judges — shimmering beings made of pure light — announced the results, <name> braced himself. He hadn’t even demonstrated his invention properly! But then, a calm voice echoed: “This year’s award for Outstanding Unity and Creative Leadership goes to… <name> of Planet Earth.”
Cheers erupted. Zilo lifted him in celebration. “Next time,” said the Martian, smiling, “bring more of those triangle snacks!” “You mean samosas?” <name> laughed. “Deal!”
As he gazed at the stars from Europa’s icy surface, <name> realized that science wasn’t just about machines or formulas — it was about hearts, minds, and the beautiful connections between worlds.
